customManagers.description: grype is not in Renovate's built-in asdf tool list, so its .tool-versions pin is invisible to the asdf manager. Track it by hand against anchore/grype releases.

packageRules.description: Pinning to a SHA keeps the SAME version you already run (just hardened), so it's not subject to the new-version stability delay — let it merge immediately.
Go module updates ship in the binary, so commit them as fix(deps) — each merged one cuts a patch release. Open a PR for review (no auto-merge).
Batch non-major Go module updates into one weekly PR.
GitHub Actions are CI tooling, not part of the binary — keep chore(deps) (no release).

Batch non-major action updates (including the initial SHA pin and digest refreshes; actions are SHA-pinned via helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests) into one weekly PR and auto-merge it once CI passes. Majors get their own PR for manual review.
Dev tools pinned in .tool-versions (golangci-lint, grype) are not part of the binary — keep chore(deps) (no release).
Batch non-major dev-tool updates into one weekly PR; auto-merge it when it only contains patch updates.

The Go toolchain ships in the binary (the stdlib is compiled in), so bumping it is a fix(deps) that cuts a release. Renovate does not bump go.mod's `go` directive by default (rangeStrategy=bump opts in); without it grype keeps flagging the old stdlib and `stack check` fails on every PR. Go point releases are security releases, so wait 3 days instead of 14.
Keep the asdf golang pin in the same PR as go.mod's `go` directive so the two never drift (CI builds with go.mod's version; `stack setup` installs the asdf one).
